description: Smart AgroNovaX by SmartBD TECH is an AI-driven agricultural robot combining NASA data with IoT. Featuring a robotic arm, soil sensors, and a camera, it automates seed sowing, planting, and irrigation. Controlled globally via SIM, Wi-Fi, or web, it includes an anti-theft tilt alarm with SMS alerts to maximize farm yield, security, and operational efficiency.
summary:
Smart AgroNovaX (AGRIBOT) is an autonomous, solar-powered agricultural rover paired with a NASA Earth-observation decision engine, developed by Team SmartBD TECH for the Field Shift challenge.
We developed a multi-functional field robot built on a triple-microcontroller architecture—combining a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (running ROS, AI voice control, and live WebRTC streaming), an Arduino UNO (operating precision irrigation, seed dispensing, weed cutting, and soil/microclimate sensors), and an ESP32 (GPS tracking and RFID security), safeguarded by SIM900A GSM fire and anti-theft alerts.
To address the Field Shift challenge, our platform fuses AGRIBOT’s real-time ground soil-moisture and climate telemetry with NASA SMAP soil-moisture and NASA GPM precipitation datasets to evaluate adaptive crop-rotation strategies (such as shifting from monocrop rice to nitrogen-fixing mungbean or drought-resilient maize).
This solution is vital because erratic rainfall and soil degradation threaten smallholder farmers. By turning complex NASA satellite data into automated fieldwork and actionable planting guidance, Smart AgroNovaX conserves water, restores soil fertility, reduces labor, and strengthens climate resilience.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works Smart AgroNovaX (AGRIBOT) is an autonomous, solar-powered agricultural rover integrated with a NASA Earth-observation decision engine, built by Team SmartBD TECH for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge.

The system operates as a closed-loop "orbit-to-soil" platform in two stages:

  1. Orbital + Ground Data Fusion: Our software ingests NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) surface/root-zone moisture data and NASA GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) rainfall forecasts, fusing them with real-time hyper-local measurements collected directly from the farm by AGRIBOT’s onboard soil moisture and microclimate sensors.
  2. Adaptive Decision & Autonomous Execution: Based on combined moisture trends and precipitation risks, the decision engine evaluates three crop-rotation pathways—comparing water-intensive continuous monocrop rice against a recommended nitrogen-fixing Rice-to-Mungbean rotation and a Drought-Tolerant Maize alternative. Once a strategy is selected, AGRIBOT autonomously navigates crop rows using an articulated 4-DOF robotic arm to dispense seeds, deliver precision water misting, and clear weeds.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Hardware & Triple-MCU Architecture:
    • Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W: Runs ROS (Robot Operating System), AI voice commands, live WebRTC video streaming, and NASA dataset processing.
    • Arduino UNO: Manages real-time motor control, the 4-DOF robotic arm, seed dispenser, precision water pump, weed cutter, and environmental sensors (soil moisture, DHT22 temperature/humidity, HC-SR04 ultrasonic obstacle avoidance, and optical flame detection).
    • ESP32: Handles wireless telemetry, NEO-6M GPS geolocation tracking, and RFID access control.
    • SIM900A GSM & Solar Power: Provides off-grid solar charging and instant SMS/call alerts for fire hazards or anti-theft security in areas without internet connectivity.
    • Custom PCB: Designed a custom 2-layer AGRIBOT All-In-One Motherboard V1.0 in KiCad 10.0.8 and Freerouting.
    • Coding Languages: Python (NASA data ingestion, ROS nodes, AI logic), C/C++ (Arduino & ESP32 embedded firmware), and HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (real-time telemetry and crop-rotation comparison dashboard).
    • Datasets: NASA SMAP Soil Moisture and NASA GPM Precipitation datasets.

What Makes Smart AgroNovaX Creative Most agricultural solutions either show farmers complex satellite charts they cannot act on, or rely on expensive heavy machinery disconnected from climate intelligence. Smart AgroNovaX bridges both worlds in a single low-cost unit—translating macro-scale NASA satellite hydrology directly into automated micro-scale field actions (planting, targeted irrigation, and rotation switching) tailored to each plot's exact soil state.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Local Manufacturability & Repairability: We engineered our KiCad motherboard with a mandatory 2 mm trace clearance matrix so the PCB can be manually fabricated, soldered, and repaired locally in Bangladesh without specialized industrial fabs, housed inside a transparent modular acrylic chassis for quick visual diagnostics.
  • Rural Connectivity & Power Constraints: Recognizing that smallholder farms often lack stable grid electricity or 4G internet, we integrated solar power harvesting alongside a SIM900A GSM fallback module so critical alerts and crop advisories reach farmers via standard cellular SMS.
  • Smallholder Affordability & Terrain: Built with a lightweight, four-wheel articulated chassis capable of traversing uneven muddy or dry deltaic soil without compacting crops.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Water & Input Conservation: Precision mist irrigation guided by NASA SMAP/GPM forecasts prevents over-watering and cuts freshwater waste.
  • Soil Regeneration & Climate Resilience: Shifting farmers from exhausting monocrop cycles to data-backed legume rotations (such as mungbean) naturally restores soil nitrogen and protects harvests against erratic monsoons and droughts.
  • Scalable Empowerment: Reduces manual labor costs and democratizes NASA Earth science for millions of smallholder farmers across Bangladesh and vulnerable agricultural deltas worldwide.
